video_title: Partial Failures: Why Distributed Systems Never Fully Succeed or Fail
core_insight: In distributed systems partial failures are normal; design to contain them and make progress with what is available instead of failing the whole request.

scenes.voice: Why does a checkout sometimes succeed halfway? In a monolith failure is binary. In distributed systems it's partial.
scenes.visual: Split screen: monolith box with green/red vs mesh of services with mixed green/yellow/red nodes.
scenes.on_screen_text: Monolith = all or nothing. Distributed = partial.

scenes.voice: A request touches API gateway, Inventory, Pricing, Recommendations. Inventory is fast, Pricing times out, Recommendations returns stale data. The request is not fully successful and not fully failed.
scenes.visual: Simple mesh diagram with API at center connecting to three services, one green, one red with timeout icon, one yellow with stale label.

scenes.voice: The obvious fix is fail fast and throw the whole request away on first error. That feels safe, but it makes availability equal to the weakest dependency and creates cascades.
scenes.visual: Chain of services breaking at one link, then whole chain turning red.

scenes.voice: Partial failure handling is detection, isolation, and graceful degradation. Timeouts and SLOs detect degradation, not just down. Bulkheads and circuit breakers isolate a slow dependency. Return best-effort with cache, defaults, or skip non-critical paths.
scenes.visual: Three icons appear sequentially: radar for detection, firewall for isolation, downward arrow for degradation.

scenes.voice: Checkout example. Inventory reserved, Shipping estimated, Payment times out. Instead of failing everything, return partial success: inventory reserved, shipping estimated, payment pending. Background reconciler heals later.
scenes.visual: Sequence diagram animating messages and partial success response.
scenes.on_screen_text: Partial success is a valid outcome
scenes.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    Client->>API: Checkout request
    API->>Inventory: reserve stock
    API->>Payment: charge card
    API->>Shipping: estimate
    Inventory-->>API: OK
    Payment-->>API: timeout
    Shipping-->>API: OK
    API-->>Client: Partial success: inventory reserved, shipping estimated. Payment pending.

scenes.voice: This trades complexity for resilience. You need timeouts, idempotency keys, fallbacks, and observability. You also accept temporary inconsistency. A hidden fallback can mask systemic problems, so signal degradation explicitly.
scenes.visual: Balance scale with Complexity on left, Resilience on right, then warning icon for silent data loss.
scenes.on_screen_text: Complexity vs resilience. Consistency vs availability

scenes.voice: Think of the system as a mesh, not a chain. Partial failures are inevitable. Contain them, define degraded but useful responses, and make operations safe for retries.
scenes.visual: Mesh network with some nodes dimmed but traffic flowing around them, ending on mental model card.
scenes.on_screen_text: Mesh, not chain. Make progress with what works.

mental_model: A distributed system is a mesh where some paths work and some don't for a window of time. Design for containment and degraded progress, not for perfect all-or-nothing success.
final_takeaway: Partial failures are normal. Isolate, degrade gracefully, and make retries safe with idempotency.
